Answer: A
Reason: In patients with pulmonary artery hypertension, chronic elevation of pulmonary pressures leads to right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation (cardiomegaly) and can weaken the pulmonary artery wall, predisposing it to pseudoaneurysm formation; thus, the cardiomegaly is likely secondary to the long-standing PA hypertension that contributed to the pseudoaneurysm.
